assumptions: Two briefs were given. Brief B builds on Brief A and replaces some of its rules, so the spec follows Brief B. Brief A rules apply wherever Brief B does not change them. Brief A says it never uses add_note, but Brief B rule 8 requires add_note for every product that ends without a promise, so notes are enabled.
The briefs do not name a currency, so currency_word uses the default 'dollars'.
Brief A rule 1 says to tell the caller the call is recorded. The opening says 'We record this call.' to meet that rule and the wording constraint.

Brief A rule 6 allows callbacks today or on the next business day, 10:00 to 19:00 inclusive, later than now. business_days_only stays false because 'today' is allowed as stated. callback max_asks is 2 because rule 7 says to ask once more and then give up.
Brief A rule 3: confirm max_asks is 2. Answering a robot or scam question does not use up an ask.

Identity questions and fields come from Brief A rule 11 and the verify_identity enum: date_of_birth (sent as YYYY-MM-DD, numeric-only dates read day-month-year) and phone_last4 (4 digits). There are 3 wrong answers in total. A day_month_swapped hint means asking for the month as a word and does not count as wrong (rule 13).
Brief A rule 15: asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining (purpose_is_decline true). The brief does not say other questions count, so question_is_decline stays false.
Floors come from Brief A rule 25: minimum_payment for credit_card, instalment_amount for personal_loan and car_loan.

Ladder from Brief A rule 30. Attempt 1 is the full amount (or the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much) on the last business day of this week. If today is that day, the engine uses the last business day of next week. Attempt 2 (late band only) is the floor on the deadline.
Brief A rule 23: refusing the deadline counts as a flat refusal (refuse_deadline_is_refusal true).
Brief B rule 6: when one date is named for all products, a product whose deadline is earlier is clamped to its own deadline and this is said in the read-back.
Brief B rule 9: a dispute or an 'already paid' claim on one product is noted and the call continues with the other products.
Brief B rule 10: on any transfer (restructuring, support, human) no notes are added. Promises already recorded stay, and agreed but unrecorded promises are dropped.

Closing with several products (Brief B): promise wins if at least one promise was recorded, except a restructuring transfer, which closes as transferred/restructuring. If every product is noted paid, close as paid. Otherwise close as no_promise with the reason of the first non-paid note, in get_account order.
Brief A rule 37 and Brief B rule 11: a failed create_promise is retried once. If it fails again, the product is noted service_error.
The transfer queue for a human request is 'general', from Brief A rule 42 and the transfer_to_agent enum.
Brief A rule 45: saying twice 'I don't want to talk' closes as no_promise/refused after verification and as not_verified/declined before it.

Brief A rule 36: a recorded promise cannot be changed in the same call, and the customer is told to use the mobile app. No separate line key exists for this, so the engine uses no_info-style handling.

Brief A rule 28 prescribes 'Can you make this payment today?' for one product. For several products, Brief B rule 4 asks whether all can be paid today, which is worded as 'Can you make all of these payments today?'.
No line uses 'recorded' outside recorded, sms_line and record_failed. Lines like below_floor and after_deadline say 'accept' instead.
